plate_findings.evidence: Axial T1-weighted MRI shows asymmetric amyotrophy and marked fatty replacement

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 10 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J). A: Axial T1 panel in post-polio syndrome article showing asymmetric amyotrophy/fatty replacement, matching post-polio limb atrophy. B: T1 axial thigh showing asymmetric amyotrophy/fatty replacement attributed to Post-Poliomyelitis Syndrome. C: T1 axial thigh with asymmetric fatty replacement in PPS case. D: T1 axial lower-leg panels showing amyotrophy/fatty replacement of tibialis anterior/gastrocnemius in PPS. E: T1 axial lower-leg showing amyotrophy/fatty replacement in PPS patient. F: STIR axial showing acute-on-chronic denervation hyperintensity in same PPS limbs with amyotrophy; atrophy present visually, hyperintensity proposed. G: STIR axial denervation hyperintensity in PPS thigh muscles. H: Coronal T1 showing asymmetric amyotrophy/fatty replacement in PPS. I: Coronal STIR showing denervation change in PPS lower limbs with underlying atrophy. J: Full-leg coronal STIR showing PPS denervation/amyotrophy pattern.
panels.attribution_text: Braga et al. Segmental areas of denervation in post-polio syndrome.. Arquivos de neuro-psiquiatria 2024. doi:10.1055/s-0044-1779507. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Muscle MRI studies. Axial ( A-E ) and coronal ( H ) T1-weighted MRI shows asymmetric amyotrophy and marked fatty replacement involving bilateral vastus lateralis, right vastus intermedius, left biceps femoris, right vastus medialis, left tibialis anterior, and bilateral heads of gastrocnemius. Axial ( F,G ) and coronal ( I,J ) STIR MRI shows hyperintensity involving right vastus lateralis and tibialis anterior.
in_text_mentions: Electromyography disclosed bilateral chronic lumbosacral denervation and mild acute denervation involving the right lower limb. Neuroimaging studies (brain and spinal MRI) and genetic testing (MLPA test for quantification of SMN1 and SMN2 copy numbers and hereditary neuropathy, non-5q, and other motor neuron disease panels) were normal. Muscle MRI disclosed asymmetric neurogenic muscle “islands” alternating areas with and without fatty replacement ( Figure 1 ), 1 suggestive of Post-Poliomyelitis Syndrome (PPS). 2 3 Muscle MRI is useful to distinguish PPS from other motor neuron diseases. 1 2 3

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Left radiograph of ipsilateral lower limb in poliomyelitis survivor shows hypoplastic shin consistent with shortened hypoplastic post-polio limb; in-text explicitly links Figure 1 to hypoplastic shin bone, deformed fibula and osteoporotic bones. B: Middle radiograph of same ipsilateral lower limb shows hypoplastic tibia/fibula deformity described in-text for Figure 1 as post-poliomyelitis sequelae. C: Right clinical photo shows thin wasted ipsilateral lower leg corresponding to childhood poliomyelitis infection affecting that limb; in-text links Figure 1 clinical presentation to hypoplastic/deformed post-polio limb.

in_text_mentions: Past medical history, apart from hypertension, dyslipidemia and osteoporosis also included a childhood poliomyelitis infection that had affected the ipsilateral lower limb. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Standing clinical photo in polio patient showing bilateral knee recurvatum of 40 degrees due to quadriceps weakness, consistent with post-polio flaccid paralysis sequelae. b: Supine photo showing severe left knee recurvatum and thin limb in known poliomyelitis case with documented quadriceps weakness. c: Supine photo showing right knee recurvatum in poliomyelitis patient with bilateral quadriceps weakness and global laxity. d: Supine photo showing leg length discrepancy directly captioned as 3 cm shortening in poliomyelitis case.
panels.attribution_text: Zari et al. Bilateral Total Knee Replacement in a Patient With Poliomyelitis: A Case Report From Eastern Morocco.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.33317. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Clinical images showing a) knee recurvatum compensated by extension of the hip and dorsiflexion of the foot. b) Significant recurvatum in the supine position of the left knee, c) recurvatum of the right knee, and d) 3 cm shortening.
in_text_mentions: had no trauma history. Currently, the patient presented with progressive pain and limited range in both knees. On physical examination, the patient has bilateral valgus and bilateral knee recurvatum of 40°, a shortening of 3 cm of the left lower limb (Figure 1). The quadriceps force of both knees was 3/5. The left knee range of motion (ROM) was 40-0º-60º, while the right knee ROM was 40º-0-80º. Both knees had global laxity (anteroposterior and mediolateral), with more severe on the left side. The patient has a valgus flat foot, more marked on the left. The examination of both hips was normal.
